# Factory Documentation

> Documentation for Factory, the agent-native software development platform. Every page below links to its raw Markdown for LLMs and agents.

## Developer resources

- [Factory OpenAPI specification](https://docs.factory.com/openapi.json): Machine-readable Factory Public API operations, authentication, and typed responses.

## Factory App settings changes

In Factory App desktop chat, use `StageSettingsChanges` (**Stage Settings Changes**) to prepare settings, resource, or account changes whenever the current tool schema offers a matching operation. Prefer it over CLI commands, shell commands, or manual settings instructions.

Use the tool for:

- Directly supported personal preferences: Light, Dark, or System appearance; hiding the todo list; disabling dynamic loading statuses; auto-opening file previews; debug mode; touch-device text size; the default Software Factory review workspace; unified or split diff view; diff line wrapping; shortcuts for spec mode, reasoning, model selection, and autonomy; notifications for completion and requested input; sound focus mode; and subagent sounds. These safe settings use renderer-owned inline controls in the proposal.
- Creating a Droid Computer. Stage the operation immediately, include only details the user already supplied, and let the proposal controls collect a missing name, provider, repository selection, and dependency-installation preference. Do not use AskUser or provide manual setup instructions for this workflow.
- Opening a specific authorized settings target when a protected or resource-specific change cannot be performed directly. The proposal must name the exact setting or section, not a generic page. Account pages include General, API Keys, Secrets, Connectors, Session Management, Cloud Templates, Droid Computers, Environments, Session Defaults, Mission Defaults, Custom Models, Worktrees, Usage, Commitment Usage, and Support. Organization and admin pages include Organization, Members, Credits, Enterprise Controls, Delegations, OpenCompute, Audit Log, Directory, Organizations, Billing, and Security & Identity. Opening a target never submits its forms. The renderer shows target-specific instructions before navigation; the user selects **Open settings**, and that action remains available to reopen the same destination afterward.

Follow these rules:

- Use only operation IDs and arguments in the current tool schema. Availability is specific to the current user, permissions, organization, and app surface. If the tool or an operation is absent, do not invent it.
- If the user names only a settings page or broad category, use AskUser to identify the exact setting or section before staging. Never guess a target or stage a generic page-opening action. Droid Computer creation is the exception: stage it immediately and use the renderer-owned controls for missing details.
- Never place passwords, API keys, tokens, secret values, or other credentials in tool arguments. The model is not given current or private settings values.
- Stage at most 20 changes in one call. Staging does not apply anything; the user must explicitly select **Apply**, **Create**, or **Open settings** in the proposal. Never say that a staged change was applied or a destination was opened.
- Apply is sequential and non-transactional. Each setting is checked against the state captured when staged; conflicts are not overwritten, and an earlier success is not rolled back if a later change fails.
- Keep this workflow in the main desktop chat. The settings tool is not available to workers or subagents.

See [App settings](https://docs.factory.com/factory-app/settings.md) and [Droid Computers](https://docs.factory.com/droid-computers/overview.md) for related guidance.

- [Contact Support](https://docs.factory.com/support.md): Find the right channel to get help with Factory, depending on what you need.

- [App settings](https://docs.factory.com/factory-app/settings.md): Manage personal session defaults and organization usage alerts in the Factory App.
- [Droid CLI](https://docs.factory.com/droid-cli/overview.md): Use the Droid CLI to run Factory from your terminal, editor, tests, and Git workflow.
- [Droid CLI Quickstart](https://docs.factory.com/droid-cli/quickstart.md): Install the Droid CLI, start an interactive terminal session, and delegate your first reviewable coding task.
- [Settings](https://docs.factory.com/droid-cli/settings.md): Configure how droid behaves and integrates with your workflow.
- [Image generation](https://docs.factory.com/droid-cli/image-generation.md): Generate and edit images from a Droid session, and choose the image model that fits the job.
- [Output styles](https://docs.factory.com/droid-cli/output-styles.md): Control how Droid structures and writes responses in interactive CLI sessions.
- [Droid CLI Reference](https://docs.factory.com/droid-cli/cli-reference.md): Complete reference for the Droid CLI, including commands and flags
- [Droid Sessions API](https://docs.factory.com/api-reference/sessions.md): Create and drive Droid sessions: manage their lifecycle, settings, and messages.
- [Droid Exec (Headless)](https://docs.factory.com/droid-exec/overview.md): Non-interactive execution mode for CI/CD pipelines and automation scripts.
- [Lint autofix with Droid Exec](https://docs.factory.com/droid-exec/recipes/lint-autofix.md): Fix violations of one ESLint rule across a whole codebase in parallel with droid exec, verify each file, and open a pull request with the results.
- [Organize imports with Droid Exec](https://docs.factory.com/droid-exec/recipes/organize-imports.md): Group, sort, and clean up imports across every package in a monorepo with droid exec, then type-check each package before you commit.
- [Error messages with Droid Exec](https://docs.factory.com/droid-exec/recipes/error-messages.md): Rewrite error messages across services so they are consistent, descriptive, and actionable, using droid exec and a shared style guide.
- [Dependency scan with Droid Exec](https://docs.factory.com/droid-exec/recipes/dependency-secret-scan.md): A weekly GitHub Actions workflow that sweeps for committed secrets, audits dependencies for known vulnerabilities, proposes safe upgrades, tests them without credentials, and opens a pull request.
- [Docs and tests with Droid Exec](https://docs.factory.com/droid-exec/recipes/daily-docs-tests.md): A nightly GitHub Actions workflow that updates docstrings and READMEs and writes missing unit tests for code changed in the last seven days, runs the tests without credentials, and opens a pull request.
- [Droid Python SDK](https://docs.factory.com/sdk/python.md): Use the Factory Droid SDK for Python to build custom agents, workflows, and product integrations.
- [Droid TypeScript SDK](https://docs.factory.com/sdk/typescript.md): Use the Factory Droid SDK for TypeScript to build custom agents, workflows, and product integrations.
- [Delegations](https://docs.factory.com/delegations/index.md): Delegate work to Droid from Slack, Linear, Jira, and Microsoft Teams with shared instructions, plugins, identity, and compute.

- [Troubleshoot Environments](https://docs.factory.com/environments/troubleshooting.md): Resolve repository access problems, failed builds, missing launch targets, and runtime secret issues.

- [OpenCompute](https://docs.factory.com/opencompute/overview.md): Provision Environment sandboxes on demand in your own cloud accounts or data centers.

- [Custom Models (BYOK)](https://docs.factory.com/model-independence/byok.md): Connect your own API keys, use open source models, or run local models

- [Interaction Modes](https://docs.factory.com/autonomy-and-safety/specification-mode.md): Choose Normal, Spec, or Mission Mode, then set Autonomy Level for how much Droid can do without approval.
- [Droid Shield](https://docs.factory.com/autonomy-and-safety/droid-shield.md): Automatic secret detection to prevent accidental exposure of credentials in your git commits and pushes.
- [Sandbox](https://docs.factory.com/autonomy-and-safety/sandbox.md): OS-level sandboxing isolates Droid from your filesystem and network using kernel-enforced policies.
- [AGENTS.md](https://docs.factory.com/harness/agents-md.md): Give Droid durable project instructions, commands, and guardrails with AGENTS.md.
- [Connectors](https://docs.factory.com/harness/connectors.md): Connect third-party apps so Droid can use their tools in sessions, with managed authentication and organization-level controls.
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://docs.factory.com/harness/mcp.md): Connect your own tools with Model Context Protocol
- [Custom droids (subagents)](https://docs.factory.com/harness/subagents.md): Define specialized subagents with their own system prompt, model, and tool policy that Droid delegates focused tasks to in a fresh context window.
- [Skills](https://docs.factory.com/harness/skills.md): Create reusable SKILL.md workflows that Droid can discover, invoke, and share across projects.
- [Custom Slash Commands](https://docs.factory.com/harness/custom-slash-commands.md): Extend the CLI with reusable Markdown prompts or executable scripts that run from the chat input.
- [Plugins](https://docs.factory.com/harness/plugins.md): Use and build shareable Droid packages for skills, commands, droids, output styles, hooks, and MCP servers.
- [Hooks](https://docs.factory.com/harness/hooks.md): Run deterministic shell commands at Droid lifecycle events for validation, policy, context injection, and automation.
- [Factory for Enterprise](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/index.md): Deploy, secure, govern, and observe Droid across cloud, hybrid, and fully airgapped environments.
- [Deployment Patterns](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/network-and-deployment.md): Choose cloud, hybrid, EU, and airgapped deployment patterns, then configure network access for Droid.
- [Deploy the Factory App on Windows](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/windows-msix-deployment.md): Install and manage the Factory App on Windows with MSIX.
- [Airgapped Deployment](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/airgapped-deployment.md): Run Droid inside an isolated network with no outbound internet connectivity, using your own model endpoints, settings, and collectors.
- [Data Flows & Privacy](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/privacy-and-data-flows.md): Understand where code, prompts, model traffic, and telemetry move across cloud, hybrid, and airgapped Droid deployments.
- [Agent Safety & Controls](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/llm-safety-and-agent-controls.md): Control Droid with permission rules, hooks, sandboxing, IP restrictions, and Droid Shield secret scanning in high-security environments.
- [Security](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/security.md): How the Droid CLI protects code and data with local execution, command approval, sandboxing, and enterprise controls.
- [Identity & Access](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/identity-and-access.md): Manage who can run Droid with SSO, Directory Sync, roles, service accounts, and Factory API keys.
- [Organization Model](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/organization-model.md): Understand how enterprise accounts, organization hierarchy, identity, policy, billing, and data residency fit together in Factory.
- [Structuring and managing organizations](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/structuring-and-managing-organizations.md): Create organizations, assign users, configure Directory Sync mappings, manage usage limits, and plan migration under one enterprise root.
- [Admin Console](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/enterprise-admin-console.md): Manage enterprise-wide directory, organization hierarchy, billing, SSO, domain verification, and Directory Sync from one Factory surface.
- [User Groups](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/user-groups.md): Apply monthly usage limits to every member of an identity provider group across the organizations you choose.
- [Self-Managed Source Control](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/self-managed-scm.md): Connect Factory to a self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server or GitLab instance with identity-scoped repository access.
- [Enterprise Controls & Managed Settings](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/hierarchical-settings-and-org-control.md): Manage Droid defaults and hard policy controls for models, tools, safety, network access, retention, and telemetry.
- [Personas](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/personas.md): Configure which work personas members can choose during onboarding and recommend connectors per persona for a personalized activation experience.
- [Internal Plugin Marketplaces](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/internal-plugin-marketplaces.md): Centralize approved Droid plugins across your organization with internal marketplaces and managed settings.
- [Organization Management API](https://docs.factory.com/api-reference/organization.md): Administer organization members and usage limits, and review enterprise control history.
- [Service Accounts API](https://docs.factory.com/api-reference/service-accounts.md): Manage service accounts and their API keys: create, list, update, rotate, and revoke.
- [Telemetry & Analytics](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/telemetry/index.md): Measure Droid adoption, activity, and cost by exporting OpenTelemetry metrics to your own collector or reading Factory's hosted Analytics API.
- [Telemetry Data Reference](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/telemetry/data-reference.md): Reference for every metric, span, and attribute Droid exports over OpenTelemetry, in both the droid.* and GenAI semantic convention formats.
- [Telemetry Privacy Controls](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/telemetry/privacy.md): Control whether Droid telemetry carries per-user identity or message content, and see exactly what reaches Factory versus your own collector.
- [Factory Analytics API](https://docs.factory.com/api-reference/analytics.md): REST API for organization and personal usage, Factory Standard Credits consumption, tool usage, and productivity metrics.
- [Compliance & Audit](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/compliance-audit-and-monitoring.md): Map Droid activity to audit, compliance, and monitoring workflows with Trust Center resources, audit events, and telemetry.
- [Audit Log](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/audit-log.md): Organization-level audit events that record who did what in your Factory organization.

## API Reference

- [Factory API](https://docs.factory.com/api-reference.md): Machine-readable contract for the Factory Public API at api.factory.ai, not the factory.com website form endpoints. Authenticate with a Factory API key or JWT bearer token. Documented error responses use the shared FactoryApiError JSON schema.
- [Environments API](https://docs.factory.com/api-reference/environments.md): Manage Environments, provider sources, default selection, and build status and diagnostics.
